answers.answer: Each player takes 12 ordinary turns: 16 spaces comprise four seasons of three ordinary rounds plus a courtship. Courtship has no player turns, no service rotation and no ongoing tile income/effects; it is only the courtship event.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; ‘Courtship is an event, with no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’

answers.answer: Host in order: rotate Quarters servants to Available, then Expended servants to Quarters (each advances one space); resolve round event, then applicable ongoing effects; choose activity; play the exact required gentry; provide all required service; resolve all positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy one tile; cleanup used servants to Expended, played gentry to personal discard, and return the tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. Only the last player advances the marker after cleanup.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Hosting an activity; Player Reference: ‘rotate service → event → ongoing effects…’

answers.answer: Pass order: all servants to Available; all gentry in personal discard to hand; event then ongoing effects; choose £200 or one free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances marker. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event…’

answers.answer: Yes. Screening is fixed at the end of step 2 when reputation is 6.1, so the PR6 activity and guests pass; later Service Help losses during the activity do not invalidate them. Service Help moves one servant only from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, for 3 reputation increments each, repeatable; it cannot refresh from Expended Service. The screening reputation is the level at the end of step 2, before Choose Activity.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions: ‘Reputation screening is fixed at the end of step 2’; Service Help row says Quarters to Available, not Expended.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; order within either group is chosen. At minimum, you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid a money penalty: the money penalty must be fully payable, and you must borrow if possible or cannot play that guest/tile if unable to fund it. Positive activity money, a money VP card, or Borrow Money can fund it.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6; Reputation, wealth and special actions: ‘A money penalty must be fully payable… You cannot take a negative favour first…’

answers.answer: Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments, gain £100, repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments, move one Quarters servant to Available, repeatable; no direct Expended-to-Available move. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments, fully refresh Market, once per turn. Special actions require sufficient reputation; at minimum 1.1 no special action may be taken.
answers.evidence: Special actions table and preceding rule: ‘At minimum you cannot… take a special action.’

answers.answer: Use Butler’s Room as a Servant Hiring activity with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service, with no fee. The room upgrades after its first use. Its upgraded option instead recruits one common footman, valet or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; it cannot recruit unique servants.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring → Butler’s Room: ‘no gentry’; ‘up to two’; upgraded room alternatively recruits one common servant.

answers.answer: Housekeeper can substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. Underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even while that regular type remains available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: substitutions paragraph.

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is purchase Butler’s Pantry; it goes from supply to Expended Service immediately, so it is not immediately available. Normally it moves to Quarters at your next rotation and Available at your second subsequent rotation. Passing or Refresh Service VP card may make it available earlier; once in Quarters, Service Help or Servants’ Quarters tile can permit earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring → Butler’s Pantry.

answers.answer: Market price is the price printed for its Market space plus the tile’s printed modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Minimum price is £100. You may not acquire a duplicate tile you already own; reputation does not limit purchasing a tile above your reputation.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Normally buy: ‘market-space price plus… modifier’; ‘Reserve base price is £300’; ‘cannot fall below £100.’

answers.answer: When an emptied Market space is refilled, slide remaining tiles left, draw replacements into rightmost spaces, and sort only newly drawn tiles by sorting number if filling multiple spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on its matching Market tile and another tile is drawn; duplicate tiles occupy one space and share its price. A Reserve-eligible tile goes straight to Reserve and another is drawn. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so no refill occurs.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Refill.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles to Reserve except Largest Wine Cellar; later drawn Service tiles also go directly to Reserve with that exception. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve and later PR1 draws go directly there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. After each of the first three courtships the Market is fully refreshed; this full seasonal refresh is standard in this summary’s rules scope.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Open Reserve and Refresh; Overview says full seasonal refresh is standard.

answers.answer: At courtship first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. In courtships 1–3, score the current face-up theme category including negative tile VP; only current face-up hybrid category counts. Highest score takes one VP card and chooses one Fairchild. If tied, each tied player draws a VP card and nobody gets a Fairchild. Each player discards one secret objective; simultaneous discards are shuffled together and placed face down at the bottom of the deck. After ordinary courtship, pass first-player marker anticlockwise.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Courtship and seasonal upkeep.

answers.answer: At final courtship, return Fairchilds and score tile VP for all four revealed themes, counting a category repeated (including negative VP) each time. Highest score gets one VP card and a Fairchild. Tie is broken by highest reputation level; wheel position is ignored. If still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards. Discard final objective; then players get a final opportunity to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible, move marker to Wedding Bells and score.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Final courtship (round 16).

answers.answer: End-game VP: all face-up printed tile VP (including unused/negative); printed gentry VP in hand and discard (family and final Fairchild included, dismissed guests excluded); fulfilled remaining objectives; reputation by level 1–7 = 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP; 2 VP per servant of any type/location; 1 VP per £200 rounded down; printed VP on retained unused VP cards. Victory ties: final Fairchild holder wins; otherwise highest reputation level wins; if still tied, shared victory. Wheel position never breaks the final game tie.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Final VP table and tie rules.

answers.answer: Normally get five objectives at setup plus two on round 6, and discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Additional objectives from Main Library or a VP-card benefit add to the retained/scoring total and do not trigger extra discards. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together, then placed face down on the bottom of the deck. Tile objectives require owning the named tile(s) at game end; upgraded sides are not required.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: ‘five at setup plus two on round 6’; courtship discard and tile objectives need not be upgraded.

answers.answer: A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later turn (multiple cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard a used card to the bottom of the VP deck; alternatively retain it hidden for its printed VP, but cannot take both benefit and VP. Retained cards score their printed VP at game end.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: VP card choice and timing.

answers.answer: Normal activity tile must flip/upgrade after first use at cleanup; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded on later uses. Hybrid starts underlined side up and flips after every use, with only face-up category counting. Ongoing-only tiles cannot host activities or upgrade. Queen’s Suite/Lionheart Suite host once then upgrade into ongoing monuments and never host again; monument income begins subsequent turns. For courtship/objectives, hybrid counts only its face-up category.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: normal tiles, hybrids, monuments and suites.

answers.answer: Monuments resolve during ongoing effects on hosting and passing turns, after the round event; each gives one reputation per ordinary turn, but none during courtship and a newly bought one first pays on a later turn. Servants’ Hall likewise resolves in ongoing effects on hosting/pass: place one Available servant to reduce one opponent by one reputation and gain one yourself; servant cannot also serve the activity and is expended at turn end. It cannot target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Monuments and Servants’ Hall.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: footman on tile, one casual guest from hand with normal guest service; double all favours, including negative; it upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite: housekeeper and one prestige guest from hand with normal service; double one chosen favour, resolve others normally; upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite: butler, draw one prestige guest to attend, no personal guest service; double nonnegative favours, negative favours excluded from doubling; keep guest and put it in discard at cleanup; upgrades into monument. Each has a fixed one-guest count that cannot be increased or decreased.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Suite activity table and following fixed-count sentence.

answers.answer: Randomly choose first player. Starting to that player’s left and going clockwise, each chooses an available base family board. Bonuses: Asquith gets Dowager Countess as fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gets £300; York gets a footman in Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Set reputation to level 1, position 1; stack 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters with 1 showing and Max at bottom; do not use 7/8 counters. Each receives butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour and Bowling Green with starter/building icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady family cards. Only Ponsonby starts with money (£300).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2, 3 and 5.

answers.answer: For three players, stock Servants for Hire with 3 valets, 3 lady’s maids, 6 footmen and 2 underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable for this game, so cannot be hired later.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: one valet and lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, two underbutlers total; unused return to box/unavailable.

answers.answer: Shuffle starter guests separately from casual deck, deal two to each player, then shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests marked with a starter icon, not a separate guest type during play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Gentry section: ‘Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon.’

answers.answer: For four players select five double-sided monuments (one per player plus one). Choose at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze, so both Estate monuments cannot be selected. Put selected monuments and all nonstarter base improvement tiles in the bag; tiles that later upgrade into monuments are included and do not count against the selection.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Opening Market has six different eligible spaces: PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible draws aside until filled, then return them to bag; stack duplicate eligible tiles in matching space. Normal tiles enter upgrade/rose hidden; hybrids underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort six spaces by ascending sorting number from the £300 space. PR4, Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal first theme face up (open courtship), keep revealed themes in order; place base Charles and Elizabeth face up. The first theme is not hidden, and old revealed themes stay in order/play as the themes accumulate.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9: ‘Reveal the first theme (open courtship); keep revealed themes in order through the game.’

answers.answer: At hosting rotation, the servant in Quarters goes first to Available Service; the servant in Expended then goes to Quarters. Each advances exactly one area. An available servant you do not use remains Available.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 1: Quarters to Available first, then Expended to Quarters; unused available servants remain available.

answers.answer: Yes, you may host Private Study later that Village Fair turn, but its unupgraded side does not earn the reward; event checks Study status before choosing/hosting. If already upgraded at the event step, gain £300 and 2 reputation immediately on spaces 3 and 9 only.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table: reward only if Study already upgraded at this step, on 3 and 9; Improvements: it need not be hosted again.

answers.answer: Resolve the round-track event after hosting service rotation (or, when passing, after servants and gentry return), before ongoing effects. On standard space 6 draw two objectives and keep both secret. Because events occur on each player’s turn at that position, passing players also receive them.
answers.evidence: Round-track events: all events use same turn order; event-before-ongoing timing; space 6 draws two.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday waives PR for all tiles and guests when hosting, so lower-reputation players may play higher-PR ones. All other requirements remain, including gentry number/type and service; other activity requirements also remain binding.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table, space 14.

answers.answer: Builders’ Holiday permits any number of Market and/or Reserve tile purchases within funds. Complete all purchases before sliding/refilling; use the unchanged Market and the prices (space/base plus modifiers) that applied before the sequence. Do not refresh between those purchases. Market Purchase VP-card benefit follows the same rule and permits any number of purchases; refill resulting empty spaces together afterward.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside while drawing replacements; fill all six spaces under normal rules, then return set-aside tiles to bag and mix. They cannot reappear during that refresh. Reserve is unchanged.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Refresh: ‘leave the Reserve unchanged’; set-aside tiles return after refill.

answers.answer: Reputation symbols are increments: clockwise gain, anticlockwise loss; crossing 5→1 raises level, 1→5 lowers level; a level spans five increments. Standard range is minimum 1.1 to maximum 7.5 (Max.5); ignore loss beyond minimum. At maximum excess is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; take special actions before or during a reputation favour to make space and avoid wasting gained reputation.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions: increment arithmetic, limits, loss handling and Max.5 rule.

answers.answer: Money is public; pay costs to and take gains from an unlimited common supply (use proxies if needed). Players cannot give or receive money from one another. You cannot spend more than you hold; cannot afford costs beyond holdings unless eligible Borrow Money obtains funds.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions: money held public; never spend more than you have; supply unlimited; no transfers.

answers.answer: Two ladies may include female family members or female guests. Two casual guests must be casual guests; family cannot satisfy that guest-type requirement. You may not play extra gentry beyond the exact count. Family requires no personal service and has no PR; female family may meet ladies requirement.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 4: exact counts/types; ladies includes females, casual requirement excludes family; family no PR/service.

answers.answer: An ordinary invite-guest favour draws the indicated guest from the matching deck, reveals it to everyone and adds it to hand (unless tile says a larger draw count). A screening invite draws stated number, selects stated number to keep, reveals only kept cards and adds them to hand; rejected cards go unrevealed to bottom of that guest deck.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: ordinary invite and screening guests.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so with no unwanted guest you need not dismiss. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity, or discard, including one drawn earlier during Enjoy Favours; family cannot be dismissed. Put dismissed guest on bottom of matching deck; it is no longer yours, is not returned on passing and does not score later.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: dismissal paragraph.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: choose screening two casual guests and keeping one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Lord has a single benefit; Lady and Heir offer choices; Dowager gives both.
answers.evidence: Base family card table.

answers.answer: Young Lady always draws one casual guest. She additionally gains two reputation only when a male prestige guest attends the same activity: that applies with the male casual guest? No—casual is not prestige, so no; female prestige does not qualify; Charles Fairchild is a male prestige guest, so yes. Her casual draw still occurs in all cases.
answers.evidence: Base family card table says male prestige guest; following text confirms Charles triggers bonus.

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest, no PR, requires valet and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest, no PR, requires lady’s maid and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. Neither has family dismissal immunity; both are guests and may be dismissed normally.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: Charles/Elizabeth details and family dismissal immunity.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent by one reputation. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and makes you lose one reputation. Minimum-reputation protection means a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: base gossips; Reputation section: minimum protection.

answers.answer: Barn gives one reputation whenever you host an Estate activity. Merely owning an Estate tile or passing does not earn it.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Barn.

answers.answer: Servants’ Quarters improvement lets you use one servant still in Quarters after normal rotation directly, in addition to Available servants, without reputation cost; servant goes to Expended at turn end. Service Help costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves one from Quarters to Available, not directly from Expended. Ordinary rotation moves all Quarters to Available then Expended to Quarters, one space each. The tile supplies at most one such direct-from-Quarters servant per turn.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring → Servants’ Quarters tile and service-mechanism table.

answers.answer: Front Private Study: one butler and two family; no tile favour. It upgrades permanently into an ongoing tile. Once upgraded it does not need to be hosted again and cannot be repeatedly hosted for Village Fair income; it gives £300 and two reputation only on Village Fair rounds 3 and 9 if already upgraded when event resolves.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Private Study; standard spaces 3 and 9.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library: one butler, two family, draw one extra objective. Upgraded: one butler, three family, draw one VP card. Extra objectives increase final retained/scoring objective count and do not cause an additional courtship discard.
answers.evidence: Improvements → Main Library; Objectives section says extras add to retained total without extra discard.

answers.answer: Objective VP card draws two objectives, keeps one, returns the other to the bottom of the objective deck. The kept one adds one additional retained/scoring objective.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards table → Objective.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service VP card moves all servants directly to Available, including Expended, and they can be used immediately. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves one servant only from Quarters to Available, never directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards table → Refresh Service.

answers.answer: Hire Servant VP card takes one servant from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutler, into Expended Service. It cannot immediately provide service from there absent another rule that changes its location; the ordinary refresh is later.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards table → Hire Servant; service movement rules.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest may return one gentry, including a family member, from personal discard to hand. If used before Invite Gentry, you may then choose that returned card to attend this activity if it meets requirements; returning alone does not play it.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards table → Refresh Guest.

answers.answer: Basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets and lady’s maids, excluding butler, housekeeper and underbutler. Ordinary end-game service VP counts every servant type/location at 2 VP each. The ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: basic-servant distinction; Final VP servants; objective table ten servants.

answers.answer: Yes. Upgraded Queen’s Suite is an Estate tile and a monument; upgraded Lionheart Suite is a Prestige tile and a monument, so each can count for monument and its category objective. Hybrids count only in their currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: monument status retains category; suite examples; hybrids rule.

answers.answer: Nature Group (11 VP): Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden or Garden Maze. Domestic Group (12 VP): Gabled Conservatory plus Main Library or North Library. Group tiles need only be owned at game end; they need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: Nature Group, Domestic Group; group-objective owning tiles suffices.

answers.answer: Prestige-guest bonus gives 1 VP per prestige guest. Every-three-guests gives 1 VP per complete three nonfamily guests; an incomplete group scores nothing. Guest excludes family; prestige guests include a final Fairchild.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: guest bonuses and definition of guest.

answers.answer: Base reputation objective awards 7 VP for maximum reputation level 7 regardless of wheel position. Wealth objective awards 10 VP for at least £1200. Ordinary reputation VP depends on level only (levels 1–7 score 1/3/6/10/15/21/28); wheel position does not alter VP or break reputation ties.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference reputation/wealth; Final VP and tie rules.

answers.answer: Both sides of base West Terrace require one butler and exactly three family. Unupgraded favour: draw one prestige guest. Upgraded favours: draw one prestige guest and optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand/current activity/discard to the bottom of their matching decks. It remains an activity on both sides and never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → West Terrace paragraph.

answers.answer: There is no hand or personal-discard limit. Gentry in discard still belong to you and score normally; passing returns them to hand unless dismissed.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: ‘There is no hand or discard-pile limit’; discard gentry score normally.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles at any time and buy any one, including one underneath another in a stack; no top-only restriction. Every Reserve tile is public. Normal prices, duplicate prohibition and purchase limits apply.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Open Reserve: ‘Every Reserve tile is public… buy any one… including a tile underneath another.’

answers.answer: No. Choose to host or pass. If preferred activity lacks required gentry or servants, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass. Exact gentry counts/types and all service requirements must be met.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Hosting an activity and Passing.

answers.answer: Yes, on a passing turn you may use the free pass-benefit Market refresh, one paid special-action refresh (cost 4 reputation increments), and multiple Market Refresh VP cards, each providing a separate refresh. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the special-action Refresh Market; pass and VP refreshes do not consume it. If you buy a tile in a Builders’ Holiday or Market Purchase VP-card buying sequence, you may not refresh between purchases in that sequence.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions: separate refresh allowances and multiple VP cards; Builders’ Holiday restriction on refresh between purchases.
